taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Ospina et al. (2020) split the Southern clade as P. collinsorum, restricting P. brachyphona to the Northern clade; Animal Diversity Web treats P. brachyphona as a single Appalachian species.
fieldMarks: Small frog; adult males 26-30 mm, females 28-34 mm.
Mostly light brown with stripes or spots of varying shades of brown along the back; a stripe from the snout across the eye.
Legs usually yellow; throat yellow to black in males and white in females.
behavior: Primarily nocturnal, also diurnal when breeding; breeding February-June, eggs in small clusters attached to vegetation.
Relatively solitary outside breeding; males defend breeding spots in vernal ponds.
Eats beetles (about 45% of diet), spiders, bugs, ants and other small invertebrates; migrates between breeding pools and upland habitat.
habitat: Wooded, hilly areas with deciduous trees; breeds in spring pools, flooded ditches, stream pools and woodland ponds.
range: Appalachian Mountains from northwestern Pennsylvania to central Alabama, generally at elevations of about 365-1066 m. Not in Canada.
